title: cert-pki values
description: Helm validates these values on lint, template and install, so a values file that names a key this chart does not read is rejected where the mistake was made rather than accepted and quietly ignored. Unknown keys are refused everywhere for that reason: the failure this guards against is a caller who renames a field and gets a silently empty rendering.

nameOverride.description: Replaces the chart name in the app.kubernetes.io/name label. Empty means the chart's own name.

fullnameOverride.description: The prefix every derived name is built from. Empty means the release name.

authorities.description: Exactly two authorities, server and client. Not an open-ended map: the certificates below are issued from these two names, so a third would render an authority nothing signs with and dropping either would leave an issuerRef pointing at nothing.

certificates.description: One entry per certificate, keyed by name. An entry carrying a client block is an mTLS pair; the chart has no notion of a mode beyond that presence.

server.description: The certificate that serves TLS, issued from the server authority. Always present.

dnsNames.description: The hosts this certificate is valid for. A server certificate with no hosts is one nothing can present.

client.description: The certificate that authenticates to a listener, issued from the client authority. Present only for an mTLS pair.

commonName.description: A client certificate names itself, because there is no hostname to name. The subject is an identity label; what authorizes it is the authority that signed it.

trustBundle.description: The ConfigMap trust-manager distributes to every namespace, and which authorities it carries.

name.description: Required, and never derived: this is the one name a workload in an unrelated namespace has to know in order to mount the roots.

authorities.description: Which of the two authorities the bundle carries. Empty renders no Bundle at all.

gateway.description: The namespace whose Gateway may reference the certificate Secrets, or null for no ReferenceGrant. Not the whole gateway contract: this chart renders no route, so a namespace is all it can use and asking for more would force a caller to invent values nothing reads.

commonName.description: The authority's subject. Required, because an authority with no name is indistinguishable from every other one in a certificate viewer.

duration.description: A Go duration as cert-manager parses it, e.g. 8760h. Hours are the only unit worth using here; minutes and seconds are accepted because cert-manager writes durations back in that form.

secretName.description: Names the object and the Secret holding it outright. Empty means the chart derives one. Setting it is how a caller knows the name without reproducing the chart's naming somewhere else, where the copy stops matching the day the formula changes.
